text:
marina: FYI escalated from CE — multiple customers seeing intermittent 502/504s for hosted inference (batch-embedding flows) over the last 20m. Customer provided request ids and short repro. Posting samples here for triage.

sam: thanks — can you paste the exact request headers + sample curl?

marina: sure, minimal repro from customer (redacted):
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACT\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-xl","inputs":["...large array..."],"batch_size":128}'
```
response: 502 from edge, sometimes 504 when stream stalls. They say it started after an auth-token rotation window at ~3743219400.

jin: ingress logs for those req ids show upstream reset + 502: `upstream reset: connection reset by peer` and a lot of `socket: too many open files` in one host. pushing full tail to gcs.

alex: sounds like pool / keepalive exhaustion on midfront. Large batch_size 128 is abusing request concurrency + long payloads holding connections open. Any auth reauth flow that would spike traffic?

marina: customer said they retried auth twice and then replayed the request batch. Sequence: token rotate -> 401 -> client retried -> auth service spiked -> midfront started returning 502.

sam: putting this on oncall. tara can you pick up host-level metrics (file descriptors, tcp connection counts) for midfront pool group midfront-prod-2 and the edge hosts that reported socket errors?

tara: grabbing metrics now. initial glance: midfront-prod-2 has FD usage at 92%, ephemeral port usage high; ingress-to-midfront concurrent sockets peaked ~8200 vs nominal 4k.

ingress-bot: automated notice: recent deploy 3743215000 to edge-ingress happened 30m before first reports; rollout stage=canary -> 25% traffic. No direct errors reported at deploy time.

alex: could be an interaction: canary changed keepalive timeout from 75s -> 15s which increases churn under long-lived streaming/batch requests. That + auth retry storm = conn churn and socket leaks.

sam: mitigation suggestions: 1) rollback keepalive change on edge-canary, 2) ask customer to reduce batch_size to 32 for now, 3) add 5s grace to auth rotate to smooth spike. Which is fastest?

marina: customer already reduced batch_size and saw immediate drop in 502s. They need a longer-term fix.

jin: I'll roll edge-canary back to previous keepalive 75s and monitor. Will also patch a prometheus alert for fd usage > 85% on midfront group.

alex: also adding a short-term gateway fallback policy: if midfront pool fd > 80% route to alt-midfront-1 until healthy. That should reduce visible 502s.

deploy-bot: rolling back edge-canary -> promoting previous build to 25% traffic...

sam: action items: jin (rollback & alert) ; alex (routing fallback + ticket for keepalive revert); tara (postmortem note + correlation of auth rota times); marina (customer comms). I'll follow up in incident ticket.

marina: thanks team — customer confirmed improved after batch reduction and rollback started. I'll keep thread updated if anything else pops. :thumbsup:

alex: follow-ups: run soak test with batch_size=128 + auth-rotate in staging to reproduce before final revert. Posting test steps in #eng-runtime.

marina: tagging customer closed-won for now; will reopen if they see further 502s.

sam: created incident runbook: https://intranet.redwood/incidents/INC-37432 (triage + RCA placeholders).

jin: monitoring dashboards show fd usage trending down now after rollback. Marking triage complete — leaving for RCA.

marina: closing thread unless new alerts.
